title: Bolna brings India’s Voice AI ecosystem together at Symphony 2026 in Bengaluru
summary: India’s flagship Voice AI summit, Symphony, gathers 1,000+ founders, enterprise leaders, investors and model labs on 20 November, with speakers from Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Y Combinator, General Catalyst and the Gates Foundation.
body_markdown:
**Bengaluru, 16 November 2026:** Bolna, the Y Combinator-backed Voice AI platform built for India, today announced Symphony 2026, India’s flagship Voice AI summit, on Friday, 20 November 2026 at The Lalit Ashok, Bengaluru. Symphony, the one-day summit will have three stages, bringing together **42+ speakers and 1,000+ attendees** from across the voice AI stack: model labs, telephony and infrastructure providers, platforms, and the enterprises running voice agents in production.


Indian enterprises handle over a billion voice calls a day across customer support, collections, recruitment, logistics and onboarding, yet much of that still runs on legacy IVR systems and human-led workflows. Building voice AI that works here is a hard problem: callers switch between languages mid-conversation, speak with regional accents and often call from noisy environments. Symphony is built around the teams solving it, and the enterprises now moving voice AI from pilots into core operations.


Bolna has built for this market from day one. It was **the only India-focused startup in its Y Combinator batch** , and in January 2026 raised a **$6.3 million seed round led by General Catalyst** , **with Y Combinator and Blume Ventures** also participating. Since its first commercial deployment in May 2025, the platform has grown **from around 1,500 calls a day to over 1.3 million calls every day** , and serves 1,000+ businesses and 50,000+ developers across 22+ Indian languages and more than 10 countries.


## Symphony at a glance


The summit is built around voice AI that is already running at scale. Highlights include:


-


**Bolna’s own models:** Bolna is **launching its in-house speech models** at Symphony, starting with an ASR model built for the short utterances common in customer calls.


-


**Trust in AI calls** : Bolna and Truecaller for Business on **raising pickup rates for AI-led calls** and building consumer trust in voice AI.


-


**Buildathon:** the winning team gets **a direct interview with Y Combinator General Partner Grey Baker** . Builders across India competed online to build anything with voice, and the top three teams pitch live at Symphony.


-


**Model integrations: new integrations with leading speech model providers** , including Kalpa Labs, giving Indian developers more models to build with on Bolna.


-


**Voice Tank:** startups pitch to investors through **a voice AI agent built on Bolna** , then the founders take live questions from investors including Blume Ventures and General Catalyst.


-


**Symphony Awards:** the India Voice AI Awards recognise the strongest deployments across enterprise, BFSI, education, e-commerce and social impact.


“If Voice AI is hard, India is the hardest version of it. A customer might pick up in Kannada, read out their account number in English and explain the problem in Hindi, on a patchy network, and the agent still has to cost less than a telecaller. In August last year we did 100,000 calls in a month for the first time; today we’re close to 40 million. That happened because a whole ecosystem was figuring out what voice can do. Today Voice AI mostly means collections calls and lead qualification. That isn’t the ceiling, it’s the current level of trust, and Symphony is about building that trust. If you build, buy or fund Voice AI, you should be in this room,” said Maitreya Wagh, Co-founder and CEO, Bolna.


“No single model can meet every enterprise's voice needs across Indian languages, and the best one keeps changing. That's why we're building Bolna as the layer that brings them all together. At Symphony, developers will see model labs, infrastructure providers and builders shaping that stack together, and what comes next: from new product updates to our own ASR models.,” said Prateek Sachan, Co-founder and CTO, Bolna.


Symphony 2026 is supported by Diamond partners Google Cloud, Truecaller for Business, Exotel and Kalpa Labs, with OpenAI and Plivo as Buildathon partners. Registration and details are available at bolna.ai/symphony.


## About Bolna


**Bolna** is a Voice AI orchestration platform that enables enterprises to build, test, deploy, and monitor human-like, multilingual AI agents at scale. Supporting **22+ Indian vernacular languages** , Bolna handles **1.3M+ daily calls** for customers across **e-commerce, logistics, BFSI, recruitment, and education sectors** . The company is backed by **General Catalyst, Y Combinator, Blume Ventures** , and operates primarily in India while serving global customers.

-

-

### Voice Tank


Voice Tank is a startup pitch with a twist. Each founder’s voice AI agent, built on Bolna, delivers a five-minute pitch on stage covering the story, the numbers and the ask. The founder then takes five minutes of live questions from investors, including Blume Ventures and General Catalyst. About 20 startups were shortlisted, and six finalists pitch live on 20 November. The format points to a future where voice agents handle longer, deeper first conversations between founders and investors.


### Buildathon


The Bolna Buildathon, run with Plivo and OpenAI, invited students, professionals and indie builders to build anything with a voice component. Teams built and submitted projects online between 15 and 31 October. The top three teams pitch at Abhyas on 20 November, with travel covered, and share ₹1.2 lakh in prizes: ₹50,000 for first place, ₹40,000 for second and ₹30,000 for third. The headline prize is **a direct interview with Y Combinator** : the winning team interviews with[Grey Baker](https://www.linkedin.com/in/greysteil/) **, General Partner at Y Combinator** , who was previously Director of Product at Figma and co-founded Dependabot, which was acquired by GitHub.
